company.name: Exemple Biosystèmes
company.description: Lyon-based startup building mechanistic AI models of the gut microbiome to predict patient response to therapies.

product.product_description: A platform that combines microbiome sequencing with clinical records to predict which patients will respond to a therapy. Hospital research teams upload stool sequencing data; the model returns response predictions with the biological pathways behind them.
product.target_market: Pharmaceutical R&D teams and university hospitals running clinical trials in gastroenterology, initially in France and Germany.
product.competitive_landscape: Competes with generic bioinformatics pipelines and with microbiome analytics providers; differs by modelling biological mechanisms rather than correlations (deck, slide 9).
product.technical_thesis: Analysis: mechanism-based models should generalise better than correlation-based ones on small clinical cohorts, which is the main constraint in microbiome trials.

methods.source_note: Product returns the pathways behind each prediction (deck, slide 7)

proprietary_technology.source_note: Deck mentions 'unique cohort data' without detail

technical.technology_differentiation: Models microbial metabolic pathways explicitly instead of learning correlations, so predictions come with a biological explanation.

strategy.current_strategy: Paid pilots with two university hospitals in 2026, then licensing to pharma trial teams.
strategy.business_model_hypothesis: Hypothesis: per-study licence fees plus usage-based pricing per analysed sample.

fundraising.fundraising_signal_summary: Founders said they will open a seed round after the hospital pilots report results.

investor_brief.investor_brief:
Exemple Biosystèmes is a Lyon spin-off modelling the gut microbiome mechanistically to predict therapy response.

It is running paid pilots with two university hospitals and plans a seed round in 2027.
investor_brief.analyst_note: One of few French teams combining mechanistic biology with clinical microbiome data.

founders.short_bio: Computational biologist, former researcher at a French public lab.
founders.bio: Camille holds a PhD in computational biology and spent five years modelling microbial communities before founding the company.

signals.title: Raises €1.5M pre-seed
signals.description: Pre-seed round led by a regional fund.

funding_rounds.notes: Investors: a regional seed fund and business angels.
